statement: The symptom is a small vibration felt in the cab at idle and light load with visible tachometer movement; felt not heard, inaudible from under the hood, no lope or stumble, idle rpm normal 650-750, identical cold and hot, present since purchase.
evidence: Owner's structured description gathered by diagnostic questioning; repeated unchanged across the whole investigation.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Symptom - as actually characterised'; CLAUDE.md 'The open problem'; [10];[15]

statement: Symptom strength tracks engine load inversely: worst in P/N at standstill (highest manifold vacuum), less in D/R, absent under road load. Rpm is not the variable; load is.
evidence: Owner's report across all gear positions; a no-load rpm sweep in Park gave roughly equal symptom at all engine speeds, so it is the arrival of load that removes it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The load relationship'; CLAUDE.md; [10]

statement: In D/R the torque converter is coupled and damps torsional pulses, therefore the engine is genuinely running rough and the converter is masking it in gear.
evidence: Original D-vs-N reasoning written into CLAUDE.md and the diagnosis doc.
reason_withdrawn: Wrong on two counts: EVERY torque-converter automatic is smoother in gear at a standstill, so the observation was never evidence of a fault; and the truck being flawless under real road load rules out the entire worsens-under-load family the reasoning pointed at.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Superseded reasoning - do not reuse'; CLAUDE.md; [28]

statement: D and R feel the same as each other, which rules out mounts, flexplate, driveshaft, U-joints, tyres and wheel balance more firmly than the old D-vs-N test.
evidence: Engine torque reacts in opposite directions in D and R, so a collapsed mount or a torque-reaction contact would feel different between them; plus the symptom reproduces at a standstill in Park.
reason_withdrawn: Sound only for torque-reaction faults. It is blind to a mount that has lost its damping, which is not direction-dependent. Mounts were later un-eliminated on that ground.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The better mount test'; CLAUDE.md; [225]

statement: Whether this is a fault at all is not established, and must be settled before more money is spent - a base regular-cab XL with a 60-degree V6 may simply feel like this.
evidence: Never smooth in the owner's entire ownership; zero powertrain codes; normal idle rpm; perfect under load; six competent repairs at six different systems all changed nothing.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Is this a fault?'; CLAUDE.md 'First question: is this a fault at all?'

statement: Two free tests settle the is-it-a-fault question: a control sample on another 2011-2014 3.7 at warm idle, and quantifying the rpm movement (plus/minus 25-50 rpm normal, plus/minus 100 rpm or a rhythmic hunt a real fault).
evidence: Stated threshold in the diagnosis doc and enforced in the tool (analysis.RPM_HUNT_MIN_P2P = 30.0).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The two tests that settle it'; CLAUDE.md; [173]

statement: The control sample on another 2011-2014 F-150 or Mustang 3.7 has never been obtained and is now the single most decisive free test remaining.
evidence: No other 3.7 has ever been measured, so whether plus/minus 25 rpm in Park and a plus/minus 1.5 percent commanded AFR dither are ordinary for this engine is genuinely unknown.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Is this dither abnormal?'; [222];[264]

statement: Six competent repairs aimed at six different systems all changed nothing, and the simplest explanation for a fault that resists every repair is that there is no fault.
evidence: Plugs, air filter, oil and filter, coolant flush, 6R80 fluid, throttle body hand-cleaned, injectors flow-tested, O2 sensors 'cleaned'.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The case that it is normal'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Ford's stated position on a 2011-2014 Mustang 3.7 vibration complaint large enough to reach a public petition was that it is normal operation of the engine.
evidence: Search-engine summary only. The described symptom is 2200-2800 rpm and shifter vibration, not this truck's idle symptom, but it bears on whether a 3.7 vibration is considered a fault at all.
source: CLAUDE.md 'Same engine, other models'; docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Research note'; [69]

statement: Engine-level claims transfer from the Mustang 3.7 community (same Cyclone engine) - phasers, chain, water pump, PCV, purge valve, fuel-trim behaviour - but vehicle-level ones do not: mounts, driveline, exhaust, cab, NVH, installation and routing.
evidence: Method rule adopted after the owner asked for all Ford 3.7 V6 information regardless of model.
source: CLAUDE.md 'Same engine, other models'; [69];[85];[173]

statement: The brother's report that it also shakes in D and R but in a different pattern contradicts the 'less in D/R' claim.
evidence: Owner relayed his brother's impression after driving the truck.
reason_withdrawn: Not actually a contradiction - 'less in D/R' was never 'zero in D/R'. Manifold vacuum at idle in Drive is only slightly lower than in Neutral, so the load model predicts a reduced but still present shake.

statement: There is no P-code of any kind on a complete multi-module scan - no misfire, fuel trim, VCT, lean or rich code. The PCM's own monitors have nothing to say about how this engine runs.
evidence: Complete multi-module scan with a generic scan app, engine warm, 2026-09.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Codes read - 2026-09'; CLAUDE.md 'Codes'

statement: Do not describe this truck as having 'no codes' - it has no POWERTRAIN codes, which is the claim the diagnosis actually rests on. Four inactive non-powertrain codes exist: U0422 (OBD-II + PCM), U0140 (OCS), B11D8(14) (RCM).
evidence: All four read as archive/inactive; U0422 reads 'confirmed, test failed since last DTC clear'.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Codes read'; CLAUDE.md 'Codes'

statement: Three modules complaining about the BCM, all inactive, is the signature of a voltage event rather than four independent faults - and this truck had its battery disconnected.
evidence: U0422 'invalid data from BCM', U0140 'no communication with BCM', B11D8 restraints event, all archive; timeline fits a battery disconnect and a subsequent code clear.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What the codes that are present mean'

statement: The RCM B11D8 entry is historical, not an active restraint fault - there is no airbag warning light.
evidence: Confirmed by the owner. The history report claims no accident history, but that same report got fuel type and drivetrain wrong.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The restraint entry, on its own account'

statement: Ford's exact definition of B11D8 and the meaning of the (14) sub-code were not confirmed - the sources were unreachable from this environment.
evidence: Network policy blocked every Ford/TSB source domain.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md '[VERIFY] Ford's exact definition of B11D8'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Permanent codes (Mode 0A) are the only code history a clear or a battery disconnect cannot destroy, and they have never been read on this vehicle.
evidence: Listed as outstanding in DATA-REQUESTS.md, the FIELD-SHEET (session E5), and 'Still unmeasured' in CLAUDE.md. Never captured.
source: docs/DATA-REQUESTS.md 'Outstanding - app menus'; docs/FIELD-SHEET.md E5; CLAUDE.md 'Still unmeasured'

statement: The archived DTCs U0422 / U0140 / B11D8, the monitor results, the freeze frame and the distance/warm-up counters were all erased by the KAM wipe performed alongside the purge valve replacement.
evidence: Owner disconnected the battery negative and bridged the cable to the positive post to drain capacitance.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'ADAPTIVES WERE WIPED DURING THE REPAIR'; [217]

statement: Short term fuel trim at warm idle sits between 0 and 3.13 percent, so there is no air leak of any significance - this eliminates the whole leak family (purge, PCV, brake booster, intake gaskets) by measurement rather than reasoning.
evidence: Warm idle in Park, ECT 93-94 C, 37 min run time: STFT B1 0.78 / 3.13 percent, STFT B2 0 percent; LTFT 0/0 percent.
reason_withdrawn: Snapshot short-term readings taken while long term trim was still un-relearned. The later load-cell measurement showed LTFT at +3.13/+2.34 percent at idle and 0 percent at 2000 rpm - a genuine unmetered-air leak that this reading had missed. The purge valve was subsequently proved to be it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Live data - 2026-09'; [107]

statement: Misfire monitor available and COMPLETED with DTC count 0 - it ran and it passed.
evidence: Monitor status since DTCs cleared, warm idle value read.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Live data - 2026-09'; [107]

statement: The live data is a third independent line of evidence, after the load curve and the absence of powertrain codes, that there is no engine fault to find.
evidence: Lambda 0.99, AFR 14.52, knock retard 0 deg, timing 11.5 deg, RPM 661, ECT 93-94 C, cam advance -0.06 deg, throttle tracking within 0.27 deg, catalyst temps identical both banks.
reason_withdrawn: One of four 'no fault' pillars. The pillar built on rpm stability fell when the graph axis was corrected, and the leak-family elimination fell when the load-cell slope was measured.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What this means'; CLAUDE.md; [107];[117]

statement: Long term trim reading exactly 0.0 percent on both banks is more likely NOT YET RE-LEARNED than learned-and-perfect - only 101 km and 3 warm-ups since codes were cleared, and the Fuel System monitor reads 'not completed'.
evidence: Caveat stated at the time; later confirmed when the trims learned to +3.13 / +2.34 percent after ~3 hours of run time.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Caveat on long-term trim'; [107];[194]

statement: Ethanol fuel percent reads 16.08 percent on a flex-fuel truck where ethanol content is inferred rather than sensed, and Saudi pump fuel is normally E0. Affects open-loop fuelling only, and the inference depends on the O2 sensors, which were 'cleaned' by an unknown method.
evidence: Read 16.08 percent in two separate value reads (10:26-10:33 and 01:00-01:01), unchanged. Never checked against a second tool.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Anomalies worth noting'; CLAUDE.md 'Anomalies from that scan'; [107]

statement: Commanded evaporative purge runs at ~41 percent at warm idle - normal and designed, but it invalidated the idle-quality protocol's assumption that sealing the purge port 'should change nothing at all on a healthy system'.
evidence: Value read at warm idle; protocol subsequently corrected to record commanded purge alongside the measurement and to distinguish a valve flowing when NOT commanded from flow proportional to a high command.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Correction this forced to the idle-quality protocol'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The 'EGR system' monitor reads Available/Completed even though this engine has no external EGR valve - on the 3.7 that monitor covers the internal EGR performed by cam overlap. It does not prove a valve exists.
evidence: Monitor status read at warm idle. RockAuto's catalogue is consistent: the 2014 F-150 3.5L EcoBoost lists an EGR valve control solenoid, the 3.7L does not.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'There is no external EGR valve on this engine'; CLAUDE.md 'Careful'

statement: Earlier revisions listed 'EGR stuck or leaking' as a ranked suspect and 'EGR actual position at idle' as required scan data. Both were wrong - the 3.7 Ti-VCT has no external EGR valve and likely no such PID.
evidence: The dilution mechanism survives but lives in the cam phasers.
reason_withdrawn: Factual error about the engine. [VERIFY against the service manual] is still carried on the internal-EGR claim itself.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'There is no external EGR valve on this engine'; CLAUDE.md 'Careful'

statement: Right front tyre reads 211.68 kPa against a 241 kPa door label - about 4 psi low. Unrelated to the idle, but real.
evidence: TPMS value read: LF 237.53, RF 211.68, RR outer 247.88, LR outer 247.88 kPa; rear inner both 0 (single rear wheel truck).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Tyres, unrelated but real'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Gear (AT) reads 1 at what was recorded as Park. On the 6R80 the transmission commands first gear internally even in Park, so it does not prove the truck was in Drive - but 'Park' was assumed rather than confirmed for every reading in the project.
evidence: Value read, 10:26-10:33 session. Park and Drive are known to differ in this vehicle's symptom, so the distinction matters.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Open question raised by this list'

statement: A channel can be blank in one session and live in the next. Barometric pressure, evaporative system vapor pressure and both wide-range current channels all read blank at 10:26-10:33 and all returned real values at 01:00. Do not mark a channel unsupported from one blank reading.
evidence: Direct comparison of two value-read sessions on the same vehicle and app.
source: docs/scanner-pids.md lines 25-28; contradicted by CLAUDE.md which still lists those channels as blank on this vehicle

statement: PCM odometer reads 131,313 km, matching the cluster - the history report's non-monotonic odometer is not reflected in the PCM.
evidence: Value read, 10:26-10:33 session.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Values that close out open questions'

statement: The scan app's graph x-axis is wall-clock time, so the repeating rpm pattern has a period of 3-5 minutes; that is slow load tracking and idle speed control is working correctly.
evidence: Read off the phone-app rpm graphs before the axis width was established.
reason_withdrawn: The axis was misread. The owner corrected it - 'the data is not 15 minutes use mobile clock' - and timing against the phone clock showed the screen is about 15 seconds wide with 5 s gridlines. The verdict reversed to a real 2.5-4 s rhythmic hunt. This was one of four independent 'no fault' pillars and it is gone.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'RPM stability - The correction'; CLAUDE.md; [116];[117];[173] error 7

statement: The graph screen is about 15 seconds wide, gridlines are 5 seconds, and the axis is MM:SS - settled independently by two clocks.
evidence: Across nine consecutive screenshots the graph clock ran 21:20 to 23:55 while the phone clock ran 12:48 to 12:51 - 2 min 35 s of graph against ~3 min of real time. An HH:MM reading would require 2 h 35 m to elapse in 3 minutes.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Axis width - now settled by two clocks'; CLAUDE.md 'Graph axis width'; [179]

statement: A rhythmic idle hunt with a period of about 2.5-4 seconds is present, and the tachometer needle visibly breathes at idle.
evidence: A/C OFF spans 37, 74, 38, 30, 53 rpm; A/C ON spans 64, 76, 64, 81, 75, 68 rpm; 4-6 cycles per 15 s screen; owner independently confirms the needle breathes.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'RPM stability - The measurement'; CLAUDE.md; [117]

statement: A/C on roughly doubles the amplitude but the oscillation is present with A/C off, so the compressor is not its cause.
evidence: A/C OFF 30-53 rpm band around 650; A/C ON 64-81 rpm.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The measurement'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The rpm cycle is attributable to cooling fan, purge or alternator cycling.
evidence: Attributed before the A/C state of the captures was known.
reason_withdrawn: The owner corrected it - 'this while AC on'. The traces were re-labelled as not a bare-idle measurement, and the cycle re-attributed to compressor cycling on top of an underlying oscillation.
source: [173] error 8

statement: One discrete event in five A/C-off windows: rpm dips to 606-612, holds briefly, then recovers with an overshoot to 680. It has width so it is not a dropped frame - something loaded the engine momentarily, cooling fan engagement being the obvious candidate.
evidence: One occurrence in five windows; the PCM caught it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'One discrete event'

statement: Stated honestly, the amplitude in the paired captures is a 24-34 rpm band (plus/minus 12-17 rpm around 650), tighter than the 30-53 measured earlier. This project's own tooling gates a hunt at 30 rpm peak-to-peak, so the truck sits on the line.
evidence: Paired 15 s windows read off the plotted curve. A limit cycle of plus/minus 15 rpm is something many healthy engines do.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Amplitude - stated honestly'; CLAUDE.md 'Amplitude - do not overstate it'

statement: Two readings of the rpm data remain alive and rpm alone cannot separate them: a real fault, or a normal governor limit cycle that happens to be visible in the needle.
evidence: Amplitude sits on the project's own 30 rpm p2p threshold.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Amplitude - stated honestly'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Fuel control is eliminated: short-term fuel trim never leaves plus/minus 1.56 percent, so if the closed-loop fuel loop were hunting STFT would swing plus/minus 10-20 percent in rhythm with rpm. It does not. The oxygen sensor hypothesis is eliminated.
evidence: Eight paired captures of rpm against STFT B1; session averages -0.92, -0.44, -0.17, -0.39, -0.34, -0.25, -0.61, -0.47 percent.
reason_withdrawn: Conceptual error. Short-term fuel trim is the correction applied AROUND the commanded ratio, not the mixture itself. With the dither living in the COMMAND, trim correctly sits near zero. Flat trim was never evidence of flat mixture. Fuel control is not eliminated - it is the source of the oscillation.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'This corrects an earlier claim in this file'; CLAUDE.md 'CORRECTION'; [173] error 10

statement: The consistently slightly-negative short-term trim average is a possible fuel-vapour signature.
evidence: Read off STFT trace averages of around -0.5 percent.
reason_withdrawn: Axis auto-scaling artefact - at half a percent this was reading meaning into a rounding step. STFT resolves 0.78 percent per step, so the trace was the loop dithering across two or three adjacent codes.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test B'; [133];[173] error 11

statement: METHOD: check the graph's axis range before judging amplitude. The app auto-scales the y-axis, so a near-constant value zooms in until one-LSB rounding flicker fills the screen and looks like a violent oscillation.
evidence: Two worked examples on this vehicle: the purge trace's full-height spikes span 40.40-40.78 percent (0.38 percent, one LSB = 0.392); the STFT trace's apparent square wave spans about plus/minus 1.5 percent at 0.78 percent per step. By contrast the rpm axis spans 618-703 and the trace occupies a third of it - that one is real.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Reading these graphs: check the axis before judging amplitude'; [133]

statement: Commanded evaporative purge is flat - 40.78 percent holding then stepping down one LSB at a time (40.78, 40.39, 40.30, 40.00) over about two minutes. A flat command cannot drive an oscillation, so purge is eliminated as the driver of the rpm hunt.
evidence: Paired rpm/purge captures, 15 s windows, warm idle in Park. Still holds after the valve replacement: the new valve modulates over 10-30 s while the hunt runs at 3-4 s, and five paired windows show no correlation.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test B'; CLAUDE.md 'Still OUT'

statement: The throttle never moves at idle on this engine - both the commanded channel (1.57 percent, min = max) and the actual channel (min = max on a 6.2-8.2 degree axis) are dead flat while rpm swings 40.
evidence: Four wide-axis windows; apparent movement in other windows is monotonic drift of 0.03-0.06 degrees on a zoomed axis. Re-confirmed after the repair (min = avg = max across eight windows while rpm swung 39-56).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Measured this session'; 'The throttle is still completely static'; CLAUDE.md

statement: A static throttle means the PCM is passive and something is disturbing the engine.
evidence: The original discriminator table: throttle oscillating means the governor is cycling; throttle steady while rpm oscillates means the PCM is holding still and something is disturbing the engine.
reason_withdrawn: The PCM is not passive - it holds idle with spark, its fast fine-trim lever, and leaves the air path alone. A static throttle meant the other lever was in use.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test C'; CLAUDE.md 'Measured: the governor is limit-cycling on SPARK'

statement: The PCM controls idle speed with spark, not air: timing advance oscillates 10-13.5 degrees (about 3.5 degrees p2p) in rhythm with rpm, and on a transient at graph clock 59:49 rpm surged to 723 with timing driven to 6 degrees, then fell to 614 with timing jumping to 15 degrees.
evidence: Axis check first: the timing axis spans 9.5-13.5 degrees in most windows, a real range rather than a zoom artefact.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test C - rpm against timing advance'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Nothing in this engine cycles at 3.5-4 seconds - firing is ~33 Hz, crank ~11 Hz, cam ~5.5 Hz, and the observed oscillation is ~0.28 Hz - therefore this is a feedback loop with lag, not a mechanical disturbance.
evidence: Arithmetic argument from engine orders at 650 rpm.
reason_withdrawn: Over-claimed. The argument holds for ROTATING parts but not for actuated or fluttering components, which can oscillate on a seconds timescale. The mechanical door was closed too early.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Why this is a control loop and not a mechanical disturbance'; CLAUDE.md 'Correction to an over-claim'; [146];[173] error 9

statement: Lead versus lag between spark and rpm cannot be judged by eye from screenshots of a closed loop; separating cause from effect needs the two cross-correlated on a synchronised log.
evidence: Stated as an honest limit at the time and never lifted. f150diag analyze exists to compute it; the phone app cannot provide it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Honest limit'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Variable camshaft actual advance #1 reads 0.00 to -0.06 degrees - two adjacent quantisation steps on an axis spanning six hundredths of a degree. The phaser is parked at rest and does not move; VCT is eliminated as the source of the oscillation.
evidence: Limit acknowledged at the time: intake bank 1 only, one of four phasers, though at idle all four would be parked together. Later confirmed far more strongly by Mode 06.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test D - cam phaser'; CLAUDE.md; [146]

statement: Every PCM output at warm idle is static except spark: throttle static, fuel trim plus/minus 1.5 percent, commanded purge flat, cam phaser parked, spark advance swinging 10-13.5 degrees. The OBD investigation is exhausted - there is nothing further to ask the PCM.
evidence: The scoreboard table from the first night of paired captures.
reason_withdrawn: Premature - Mode 06, the fuel-cut test, WOT breathing and the post-repair trim reads all came later and all produced new information. The genuine exhaustion of the ECU came on 2026-09-05 after Mode 06.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The scoreboard'; CLAUDE.md

statement: MAF being flat at idle (~3.01 g/s, plus/minus 1.7 percent) is expected, not suspicious: at idle the throttle is a fixed restriction with ~30 kPa manifold against ~100 kPa baro, so flow is choked and nearly independent of engine speed. Flat MAF rules nothing in or out.
evidence: Paired rpm/MAF captures at warm idle in Park.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'MAF being flat is expected'; CLAUDE.md 'Still OUT'

statement: Calculated load is derived arithmetic on MAF, rpm, baro and intake temperature, not an independent witness - with MAF constant and rpm swinging, load must swing.
evidence: Stated when the paired rpm/calculated-load capture was analysed.
source: [155]; docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Measured this session' table

statement: The mixture oscillation at idle is COMMANDED by the PCM, not a disturbance the PCM is reacting to: Fuel/Air commanded equivalence ratio is a square wave alternating between about 14.41 and 14.86 AFR (lambda ~0.98/~1.012) at the same 3.4-4 s period as everything else, and measured lambda on both banks follows it.
evidence: Paired graph captures, 15 s screens, warm idle in Park, A/C off, values read off the plotted curve. This is the shape of fore/aft catalyst control - the deliberate dither that exercises the catalyst's oxygen storage, whose period is set by how slowly the catalyst stores and releases oxygen.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Paired traces - THE PCM COMMANDS THE OSCILLATION'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The measured causal chain: PCM commands a plus/minus 1.5 percent AFR square wave, measured lambda follows (0.98-1.02 both banks), cylinder torque varies, rpm swings plus/minus 15-20 at 3.4-4 s, spark advance modulates 10-13.5 degrees to hold rpm.
evidence: Every link measured on paired graph captures.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The causal chain'; CLAUDE.md 'Paired traces'

statement: Whether the commanded plus/minus 1.5 percent AFR dither is abnormal is unknown, and that is the honest limit. It is within the range many Ford PCMs run; nothing measured says the amplitude is excessive and nothing says it is normal.
evidence: Settling it needs a control sample on another 3.7, or cross-correlation on a synchronised log - not screenshots.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Is this dither abnormal?'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Fuelling is symmetric across banks: both upstream wideband sensors report the commanded dither faithfully, fast and at equal amplitude (B1 avg 14.65, B2 avg 14.68).
evidence: Paired captures of rpm with O2S1 air:fuel (B1) and O2S5 air:fuel (B2).
reason_withdrawn: Wrong variable. The upstream sensor reads the mixture AFTER the PCM has corrected it; the trim reads HOW MUCH correction was needed. Identical lambda with different trims means the underlying fuelling is not identical. (Note: bank symmetry was nevertheless re-established later on better evidence - see F-051.)
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'This corrects fuelling is symmetric across banks'; [173] section 9

statement: The only asymmetry in the data set is downstream: bank 1's post-cat narrowband voltage swings deeper and leaner (avg 0.58-0.63 V, swing 0.17-0.82) than bank 2's (avg 0.70-0.72 V, swing 0.30-0.83), meaning bank 1's catalyst buffers less of the dither.
evidence: Paired graph captures of rpm with O2S2 voltage on each bank at warm idle.
reason_withdrawn: Definitively killed by the Mode 06 catalyst monitor: bank 1 0.3711, bank 2 0.3633 against a 0.8359 limit, both at 44 percent of threshold and within 2 percent of each other. The idle asymmetry was an artefact of reading a swinging narrowband signal at the worst operating point for judging a converter.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Bank symmetry'; 'The catalyst question is settled'; [165];[254]

statement: Do not condemn a catalyst on the downstream idle asymmetry: idle is the wrong operating point (lowest exhaust mass flow and temperature), and the slow 3.4-4 s period argues FOR intact oxygen storage - less storage would make the fore/aft loop run faster.
evidence: Reasoning recorded at the time the asymmetry was found; vindicated by Mode 06.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Do not condemn a catalyst on this'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Bank 2 short-term trim runs about +3.5 percent (stepping between 3.13 and 3.91) where bank 1 runs about 0 percent, so bank 2 needs about 3.5 percent more fuel than bank 1 to reach the same measured lambda.
evidence: Nine consecutive ~15 s windows of STFT B2 paired with rpm, warm idle in Park - a properly read curve.
reason_withdrawn: Withdrawn on two separate grounds. (1) The bank 1 figure came from the scan app's own Avg field, which is session-cumulative and already ruled inadmissible - a good number was compared against a bad one; and the corroborating bank 1 value-read came from a session about two hours earlier, which cannot be set against the graphs. (2) Long term trim later learned to +3.13 (B1) and +2.34 (B2), one quantisation step apart. What still stands is the nine windows of B2 at 3.13-3.91; what does not is that bank 1 differs from it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Bank 2 short-term trim runs +3.5 percent'; [179];[183];[194]

statement: Nothing may be concluded from a bank-to-bank trim offset until STFT B1 and STFT B2 are captured in ONE window. The leak and sensor-bias reasoning built on the offset is contingent on that capture.
evidence: Both figures came from captures taken at different points in the same session.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The test that settles the offset'; [183]

statement: THE BANK ASYMMETRY IS DEAD. Long term trim learned to +3.13 percent (B1) and +2.34 percent (B2) - a difference of 0.79 percent, exactly one quantisation step, the smallest difference the PID can express. The engine fuels both banks the same.
evidence: Value read at 01:00-01:01 phone clock, warm idle, 640 rpm, 3 h 06 m run time since engine start. Long term trim is the learned average, far better evidence than snapshots of a short term trim that swings every second.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Session 01:00-01:01 - long term trims have LEARNED'; CLAUDE.md; [194]

statement: Everything built on a bank difference is withdrawn: the bank-specific vacuum leak, the exhaust leak upstream of one sensor, and the one-sided upstream sensor bias. None survive two long term trims within one LSB of each other.
evidence: LTFT +3.13 / +2.34 percent at idle.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Session 01:00-01:01'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The downstream O2 asymmetry is weak and unconfirmed even before Mode 06: snapshots at 01:00 show B1 at 0.79 V and B2 moving 0.67 to 0.79 V between screens, so the ranges overlap heavily and a single value carries no information.
evidence: Value-read snapshots, 01:00-01:01 session.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Downstream oxygen sensor snapshots'

statement: What replaces the bank asymmetry is a small, EVEN lean bias of about +2.3 to +3.1 percent on both banks - small (plus/minus 10 percent is normal, sets no code) but learned and even.
evidence: LTFT +3.13 / +2.34 percent, warm idle, 640 rpm, after 3 h 06 m run time.
reason_withdrawn: The bias was subsequently traced to the EVAP purge valve and eliminated: after the new valve and a relearning drive, both banks read -0.78 percent at warm idle in Park.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What replaces it'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Barometric pressure reads 97 kPa where Jeddah is at sea level and standard is 101.3 kPa - about 4 percent low. Ford derives baro from the MAP sensor, and a low reading would make the PCM under-fuel with the O2 sensors adding it back, which is the direction and roughly the magnitude of the measured lean bias.
evidence: Value read, 01:00-01:01 session. Two things unchecked: the actual local pressure at that hour, and how heavily a MAF-based strategy weights the baro term - on a mass-flow system baro is a correction, not the primary input, so a 4 percent error there should not give 4 percent of fuelling error.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Barometric pressure reads 97 kPa'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Load separates a leak from a calibration offset: a leak is a fixed hole whose trim contribution shrinks as the throttle opens, while a MAF or barometric error is proportional and stays constant at every load. Ford stores long term trim in separate cells by load, so reading it at idle and at 2000 rpm reads both cells directly.
evidence: Reasoning stated before the 2000 rpm test and then confirmed by it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The test that separates a leak from a calibration offset is load'; CLAUDE.md

statement: ECU voltage averaged 12.62 V with the engine running (min 12.39, max 12.82 across four captures), in a session where other windows minutes apart read 13.76-14.0 V. Either Ford smart charging or the alternator has stopped charging.
evidence: Paired rpm / ECU voltage graph captures.
reason_withdrawn: Answered by the BCM data: state of charge rose 88 to 90 percent and then charging stopped. A failed alternator cannot raise state of charge.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Open, from this session'; [161];[173]

statement: The charging question is ANSWERED - this is Ford's smart charging strategy, not a failed alternator. Battery SoC rose from 88 to 90 percent between sessions and then current fell to 0 A with voltage settling to battery level.
evidence: [BCM] Vehicle Battery Voltage 13.8 V / 12.8 V, [BCM] Vehicle Battery Current 1 A / 0 A, [BCM] Battery SoC 88 / 90 percent across the 10:26-10:33 and 01:00-01:01 sessions. The truck has a battery monitoring sensor on the negative cable.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The charging question is answered'; CLAUDE.md 'Charging: ANSWERED'; [183]

statement: AC ripple across the battery (under 0.1 V AC) and three ground voltage drops (each under 0.1 V) remain worth doing on their own merits even though the charging item is closed.
evidence: Deferred at the owner's request - 'any thing required multimeter save it and will do it tomorrow'. Never performed.
source: docs/DATA-REQUESTS.md 'Physical tests'; CLAUDE.md 'Next - all physical'; [173]

statement: RULE: total fuel correction = short term trim + long term trim. When long term rises, short term falls by the same amount. Neither trim number means anything on its own - always capture BOTH halves of the SAME bank.
evidence: Four consecutive windows at 01:12-01:13: LTFT B2 perfectly flat at 2.34 percent while STFT B1 walked from 0 to about -1.6 percent over 70 s in 0.78 percent steps. At 01:00 LTFT B1 +3.13 with STFT B1 0 gave a total of +3.1 percent; at 01:13 LTFT B1 inferred ~+4.5 with STFT B1 -1.4 gave the same ~+3.1 percent total.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Session 01:12-01:13 - the trims are handing off'; CLAUDE.md 'Trims trade off'

statement: A short-term trim going negative is the signature of successful learning, not of the mixture changing. The +3 percent total is confirmed, not contradicted, by it.
evidence: STFT B1 drifting to -1.6 percent while the total held at about +3.1 percent.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Consequences'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Long term fuel trim on this PCM is INDEXED BY LOAD and the displayed number is whichever cell is currently active - it left its idle value on throttle opening and returned to the identical value on throttle closing, instantly, with no re-learning interval.
evidence: Two independent captures two hours apart in graph time, on both banks. Bank 2 alone at 01:18-01:20 (2.34 to 0 to exactly 2.34); both banks at 01:30-01:32 (B1 3.13 to 0 to 3.12, B2 2.34 to 0 to 2.34, final window min = avg = max).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE 2000 RPM LOAD TEST'; 'The load-cell mechanism, now beyond doubt'; [199];[202]

statement: The engine runs lean at idle and stops running lean as soon as the throttle opens - the signature of unmetered air entering downstream of the MAF, i.e. a vacuum leak.
evidence: Learned correction: idle +3.13 (B1) / +2.34 (B2) percent, ~2000 rpm 0 percent on both banks. A fixed-size opening is a large fraction of idle airflow and negligible at 2000 rpm; a MAF or baro calibration error would stay constant across both cells.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE 2000 RPM LOAD TEST'; CLAUDE.md; [199];[202]

statement: The learned correction is a GRADIENT, not a step: idle +3.13/+2.34 percent, just above idle +0.78 percent, ~2000 rpm 0 percent. The correction fades smoothly as airflow rises - the behaviour of a fixed-size opening, not of a proportional MAF or baro error.
evidence: During the 2 min 7 s hold, LTFT B1 repeatedly flicked to 0.78 percent and back (B2 less often) as the rpm wandered across load-cell boundaries. This slope is stronger evidence than the two endpoints alone and substantially weakens the un-learned-cell objection - cells across the range hold distinct, ordered, non-zero values.
reason_withdrawn: The whole slope was learned around the OLD purge valve and was erased by the KAM wipe performed with the replacement. It must be re-measured from scratch; it has not been.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'CONFIRMED ON BOTH BANKS'; CLAUDE.md; [202];[217]

statement: The lean measurement matches the symptom's own load curve - highest vacuum gives the worst shake, throttle open removes it. It is the first measured finding in this investigation whose shape matches the complaint.
evidence: Load curve from the owner's description arrived at independently from the trim cells.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'It matches the symptom's own shape'; CLAUDE.md

statement: CAVEAT: the 0 percent load cell could be un-learned rather than learned - only 101 km and 3 warm-ups since the codes were cleared. Close it by re-reading after 15-20 minutes of real driving.
evidence: Stated as the honest caveat at the time. Substantially weakened by the discovery of the ordered slope, and the drive was subsequently performed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The honest caveat, and how to close it'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The STFT B1 trace during the 2000 rpm hold is recorded but NOT interpreted - it is the wrong pairing (bank 1 short term against bank 2 long term gives no bank's total) and the throttle was hand-held with the rpm unrecorded.
evidence: Ten windows of STFT B1 centres from -4.5 to +3.5 percent during the hold. The finding rests on the long term cell values alone, which do not depend on either objection.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'STFT B1 during the hold - recorded, not over-read'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The +9.38 percent STFT B1 spike on tip-in and the -11.72 percent crash on throttle closure are ordinary transient enrichment and overrun behaviour, and they timestamp the throttle events precisely against the long term trim's cell changes.
evidence: Graph clock 51:17 and 53:45 in the 01:18-01:20 capture.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The two spikes in STFT B1'; CLAUDE.md

statement: A smoke test is now justified - earlier revisions said trims did not warrant one, which was correct when long term trim read 0 percent and was believed un-learned.
evidence: LTFT +2.34 percent at idle and 0 percent at load is precisely the pattern a smoke test is designed to locate.
reason_withdrawn: Withdrawn again after the purge valve replacement and the relearning drive: idle trim read -0.78 percent on both banks, so there is no lean bias left for a smoke test to explain.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'A smoke test is now justified'; 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; [200];[251]

statement: If the leak is uneven - feeding one runner more than the others - it would also explain the felt vibration: the bank average moves only 2-3 percent (too little to code) while the affected cylinder runs materially leaner and contributes a weaker power stroke once per engine cycle, at ~5.5 Hz (half engine speed) at this idle.
evidence: Hypothesis raised to connect the measured lean bias to the felt shake.
reason_withdrawn: The lean bias was eliminated by the purge valve replacement, and Mode 06 per-cylinder misfire counts (0,0,0,2,0,1 with a zero ten-cycle EWMA on all six) plus the rpm sweep (no worsening between 1000 and 1800 rpm) both eliminate the single-weak-cylinder mechanism.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'If the leak is uneven'; CLAUDE.md; [247];[254]

statement: Owner's observation: the rpm would not hold steady at 2000. Two ordinary explanations - the throttle is drive-by-wire so a steady foot is not a steady plate, and coolant at 98 C means the fan is cycling and loading the engine.
evidence: Recorded because it was reported. It does not affect the trim finding, which rests on learned cell values. Worth its own capture: Engine RPM + Throttle Position Actually at a held 2000 rpm - never taken.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The owner's observation: rpm would not hold steady at 2000'; [201];[202]

statement: PURGE VALVE REPLACED: the shake is GONE in D and R and still present in P and N. This is the first change in the symptom in the owner's entire ownership.
evidence: Owner's report after fitting a new EVAP purge valve. Six previous repairs aimed at six different systems changed nothing measurable; this one moved the symptom boundary, exactly as the trim slope predicted.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'PURGE VALVE REPLACED'; CLAUDE.md; [206];[207]

statement: The EVAP purge valve was a real contributor and is confirmed as a genuine source of unmetered air on this vehicle.
evidence: Trim slope before the repair (+3.13/+2.34 at idle, 0 at 2000 rpm), symptom boundary moved after it, and idle trim measured at -0.78 percent on both banks after the relearning drive.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What this establishes'; [252];[264]

statement: The remaining shake sits in the condition with the HIGHEST manifold vacuum, so the symptom still tracks vacuum inversely and at least one more unmetered-air source remains.
evidence: Reasoning immediately after the purge valve replacement, before the adaptives had relearned.
reason_withdrawn: After the relearning drive, long term trim at warm idle in Park read -0.78 percent on BOTH banks - identical, dead flat, three windows. There is no lean bias left, so there is no second unmetered-air source to find. The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'And it is not the whole story'; CLAUDE.md; [207];[251]

statement: The truck is now its own control: P/N shakes and D/R is clean, minutes apart, same engine, same temperature. Every remaining question should be asked as 'how does P differ from D at a standstill'.
evidence: Sharp symptom boundary at a standstill after the repair, where previously every condition sat on a continuum.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The truck is now its own control'; CLAUDE.md; [207]

statement: Long term trim learned to zero after the repair, so the leak is gone.
evidence: Both banks read 0 percent at idle immediately after the purge valve replacement.
reason_withdrawn: The memory was ERASED, not learned. The owner disconnected the battery negative and bridged the cable to the positive post to drain capacitance - a full Keep Alive Memory wipe - at the same time as fitting the valve. The number carries no information until the truck has been driven.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'ADAPTIVES WERE WIPED DURING THE REPAIR'; CLAUDE.md; [216];[217]

statement: Short term trim survives a KAM wipe because it is a live correction that does not depend on anything learned - with long term at 0, short term IS the entire correction requested. Before the valve +3.13 LT / ~0 ST = +3.1 percent total; after the valve 0 LT (wiped) / -1.5 ST = -1.5 percent total, a swing of about 4.6 points.
evidence: Warm idle in Park, before and after. The engine genuinely no longer runs lean at idle; only the long term numbers supporting that were unusable.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What survives, and it is the part that matters'; CLAUDE.md; [217]

statement: CONFOUND: the new valve was fitted AND the adaptives were wiped in one operation, so the D/R improvement has two candidate causes. Against the reset being responsible - the owner already performed a relearn and drove 300 km earlier with no change, so a reset alone has been tried and has already failed.
evidence: Close it by letting the adaptives relearn: if the improvement came from the reset, the shake returns in D and R as long term re-learns. The subsequent drive relearned the trims to -0.78 percent and D/R stayed clean.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The confound this creates'; CLAUDE.md; [217]

statement: RULE: never wipe Keep Alive Memory before a measurement unless the wipe is itself the experiment. It destroys learned trims, code history, freeze frames and monitor results in one action, and it puts a second variable into any repair performed at the same time.
evidence: Established after the purge valve replacement destroyed the pre-repair load-cell slope, the archived DTCs, the monitors and Mode 06 in one operation.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Rule going forward'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Confirm the D/R improvement survives a heat cycle before treating it as permanent - 'less' becoming 'gone' is a change in degree reported by feel.
evidence: Caveat recorded at the time of the repair; a cold-start re-check was never reported.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Caveats to hold'; CLAUDE.md

statement: PARK vs DRIVE, same session, minutes apart: Park idles at ~650 rpm with spans of 44, 55, 53, 50 rpm in a clean regular repeating shape at ~3.4-3.5 s and 4.5 degrees of timing swing; Drive idles at ~550 rpm with spans of 15, 13, 18 rpm, unstructured, no rhythm, 2 degrees of timing swing.
evidence: Engine RPM paired with Tim. adv., warm, standstill, four windows in Drive on the brake and five in Park, 03:23-03:25 phone clock. The first clean within-vehicle comparison in the investigation. Peaks in the 16:03 window at ~16:07.5, 16:11, 16:14.5, 16:18 - four evenly spaced humps.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'PARK vs DRIVE, SAME SESSION'; CLAUDE.md; [219];[221];[222]

statement: The hunt and the felt shake are ONE phenomenon - they appear together in Park and vanish together in Drive, so there is one thing to explain, not two.
evidence: Park/Drive comparison in one session.
reason_withdrawn: The owner corrected it: the shake moves him in the seat. A plus/minus 25 rpm swing at 3.4 s is a 4 percent cycling of engine speed - it moves a needle, it does not move a person. And the inference was weak anyway: the torque converter damps EVERYTHING in gear, so 'both vanish in D' never distinguished them.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What this settles'; 'CORRECTION - the shake is STRONG'; CLAUDE.md; [222];[224];[225]

statement: The hunt (~0.28 Hz, scan-tool visible) and the felt shake (firing pulse ~33 Hz, invisible to OBD) are two separate observations.
evidence: Originally stated on the first night, briefly withdrawn when Park/Drive showed them co-occurring, then restored when the owner reported the shake is strong enough to move him in the seat.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Does this explain the felt vibration?'; 'CORRECTION - the shake is STRONG'; [225]

statement: Ford commands roughly 100 rpm lower idle in gear by design, so the ~550 rpm in Drive against ~650 in Park is not a fault.
evidence: Measured across the Park/Drive comparison.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'PARK vs DRIVE'; [220]

statement: The Park-versus-Drive difference is ALSO exactly what every healthy torque-converter automatic does: in gear the converter loads and damps the engine, so the same torque disturbance moves the speed far less, and a loop that limit-cycles unloaded can be stable loaded.
evidence: Coherent picture with every element measured: PCM commands the dither, torque ripples, Park unloaded gives plus/minus 25 rpm and Drive converter-loaded gives plus/minus 8 rpm.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What this does NOT settle'; CLAUDE.md; [222]

statement: The accelerometer test changes meaning: it should look for a ~0.28 Hz AMPLITUDE MODULATION of the firing pulse - vibration strength rising and falling every ~3.4 s - as well as for fixed frequencies, and be captured in Park and in Drive.
evidence: Consequence of the Park/Drive finding. Never performed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Consequences for the remaining work'; CLAUDE.md; [223]

statement: MOUNTS ARE NOT ELIMINATED. The D-versus-R test rules out torque-reaction faults (a collapsed mount would load differently in D than R) but is blind to a mount that has lost its DAMPING, which is not direction-dependent.
evidence: The engine rocks on its mounts at 8-15 Hz at idle - felt through a seat, not heard. Fluid-filled mounts exist to damp exactly that mode; one that loses its fluid stops damping it. In gear, converter drag preloads the engine against the mounts, shifting it millimetres and changing the rocking mode.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'This un-eliminates the mounts'; CLAUDE.md 'MOUNTS ARE NOT ELIMINATED'; [225]

statement: Whether the 2014 F-150 3.7 uses hydraulic (fluid-filled) engine mounts is not confirmed against the service manual.
evidence: The mount-damping hypothesis depends on it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md '[VERIFY] whether the 2014 F-150 3.7 uses hydraulic mounts'; CLAUDE.md

statement: SECOND CANDIDATE, raised far too late: CONTACT. Something resting against the frame or cab - exhaust pipe, A/C line, power steering line, cooler line, wiring loom, heat shield. Shifting into gear rotates the engine slightly and a part that merely touches at rest breaks contact.
evidence: Gives strong in P, gone in D, felt not heard, invisible to every sensor, present since purchase, and unaffected by plugs, injectors, throttle body, coolant and fluid changes. Consistent with three nights of OBD work finding a real but small fuel fault and nothing that explains a strong vibration.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Second candidate, which should have been raised much earlier: contact'; CLAUDE.md; [225]

statement: STANDING LESSON: the owner's description of the symptom outranks an inference drawn from graphs. Two conclusions have been withdrawn because a measured correlation was allowed to override what the vehicle actually does - the converter-damping argument early on, and the one-phenomenon argument later.
evidence: Both withdrawals recorded in the diagnosis doc.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Standing lesson'; CLAUDE.md; [225];[226]

statement: The NEUTRAL COAST test (engine at idle with the truck moving, to isolate the vibration path from the engine) is withdrawn - it does not work.
evidence: Proposed in docs/DRIVING-TESTS.md as a way to separate the vibration path from the engine.
reason_withdrawn: The owner found two faults with it and both are correct: shifting to N above a road-speed threshold makes the PCM raise idle, so the engine is not in the same state at all; and road and tyre vibration at 60 km/h swamps a small idle shake. Replaced by the rpm sweep in Park.
source: CLAUDE.md 'The neutral coast is WITHDRAWN'; [244];[245]

statement: RPM SWEEP IN PARK, owner's result: worst at idle 650, no worsening anywhere between 1000 and 1800, and no growth with rpm.
evidence: Owner's own subjective sweep, holding rpm and rating the shake.
source: [246];[247]; CLAUDE.md 'RPM SWEEP IN PARK'

statement: The rpm sweep result rules out half-order excitation (one cylinder differing, which would worsen sweeping into the 8-15 Hz mount band around 1000-1800 rpm) and rules out rotational imbalance driving the cab directly (which would grow continuously with rpm).
evidence: Prediction stated before the test and failed. Not conclusive on its own; Mode 06 settled the single-cylinder question directly.
source: [247]; docs/f150-diagnosis.md rpm-sweep table; CLAUDE.md

statement: The leading mechanical explanation: at 650 rpm first order is 10.8 Hz, and the engine rocking on its mounts resonates at roughly 8-15 Hz, so idle sits dead centre of that band. As revs rise first order climbs out of the band; in gear converter preload shifts and damps the mode.
evidence: One mechanism explaining worst at idle, better as rpm rises, gone in D and R, no codes and nothing on any sensor, present since purchase, and six fuel/ignition repairs changing nothing. A 60-degree V6 has an inherent once-per-revolution rocking couple normally absorbed by the counterweights, the harmonic damper and the mounts.

statement: The harmonic balancer (crank pulley damper) is a live candidate: twelve years of Jeddah heat degrades the rubber bonding the outer ring to the hub, the ring creeps, and first-order imbalance appears out of nothing.
evidence: Check engine-off for concentricity and rubber condition, then watch it spin at idle with a light or timing light - a good one spins true, a failed one visibly wobbles. Never performed.

statement: The remaining hands-on tests, all free: touch test across the mount (engine, frame rail, cab floor); watch the engine rock through P-D-R-P; hunt for a contact point by hand and push/pull it while someone reports the seat; pry-bar each mount in turn while idling; accelerometer to name the frequency family (~10 Hz mount rock, ~11 Hz rotational imbalance, ~5.5 Hz one weak cylinder, ~33 Hz firing pulse meaning an isolation problem).
evidence: All specified; none reported as performed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The tests, all free, all hands-on'; CLAUDE.md; [225];[226]

statement: ELECTRICAL LOAD AT IDLE IN PARK - all loads on, since alternator drag is a mild version of what the converter does in D. Shake reduces means load damping is the mechanism; no change means the D/R difference comes from engine position or a contact that breaks in gear.
evidence: Proposed test. Never performed.
source: CLAUDE.md 'ELECTRICAL LOAD AT IDLE IN PARK'

statement: DECELERATION FUEL CUT, bank 1: O2S1 air:fuel steps vertically to 29.38 (top of the PID's range) the instant the throttle closes and holds min = avg = max across three consecutive windows from ~1850 rpm down to ~850 rpm. Nothing is putting fuel into bank 1 during overrun.
evidence: Coasting in gear from ~100 km/h to 30 with the throttle shut, Engine RPM paired with O2S1 air:fuel, 03:49-03:50. The dips and spikes in rpm during the coast are downshifts, normal.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'DECELERATION FUEL CUT'; CLAUDE.md; [233]

statement: The fuel cut test is the best oxygen sensor test in this investigation: the bank 1 upstream sensor moved 13.49 to 29.38 in a fraction of a second, held it perfectly flat for a minute, and repeated it. A lazy or contaminated sensor cannot do that.
evidence: This closes the 'O2 sensors cleaned by an unknown method' concern carried open since the start of the project. Idle data could never demonstrate it because the mixture never leaves a narrow band there.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'It is also the best oxygen sensor test'; CLAUDE.md; [233]

statement: Bank 2 does exactly the same on fuel cut: O2S5 air:fuel pegs at 29.38 flat, min = avg = max across two windows while rpm falls 1772 to 1381, and it swept even wider than bank 1 - 12.33 (power enrichment) to 29.38, fast in both directions.
evidence: Same coast, 03:58 phone clock.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Bank 2 - same result'; CLAUDE.md; [238]

statement: THE FUEL SYSTEM IS ELIMINATED: leaking injectors on both banks out, both upstream oxygen sensors confirmed healthy across full range, and fuel delivery under load proven (about 12.3:1 commanded and delivered at wide throttle, exercising pump, regulator and injectors).
evidence: Fuel cut on both banks plus WOT AFR, plus trims near zero at idle after the new purge valve.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Bank 2 - same result. THE FUEL SYSTEM IS ELIMINATED'; CLAUDE.md; [238];[241]

statement: WIDE OPEN THROTTLE: the engine breathes perfectly. Abs. load peaks at 96.47 percent (sustained 91-94 percent), MAF peaks at 215.27 g/sec, and rpm pulls cleanly to 6832 with the MAF curve rising smoothly and linearly from 10 to 215 g/s with NO plateau, falling only on lift.
evidence: Full-throttle pulls captured as Abs. load + Engine RPM then MAF + Engine RPM, 04:02-04:03. A restriction shows as airflow going flat while rpm keeps rising; this engine does not do that. Healthy target is 90-100 percent absolute load on a naturally aspirated engine.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'WIDE OPEN THROTTLE'; CLAUDE.md; [241]

statement: Cross-check: peak airflow in g/s times roughly 1.4 approximates crank horsepower on a naturally aspirated petrol engine, so 215 x 1.4 is about 301 hp against a factory rating of 302.
evidence: Explicitly flagged as a rule of thumb, not a verified specification.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Cross-check'; CLAUDE.md

statement: Long term trims after the drive read -1.56 percent (B1) and -0.78 percent (B2), both flat with min = avg = max, one quantisation step apart, both essentially zero and slightly negative. The +3.13/+2.34 percent lean bias is gone.
evidence: Captured 04:04-04:05 after the drive. In a later window they drift one step closer to zero still (-0.78 and 0).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Long term trims after the drive'; CLAUDE.md

statement: The operating condition during the 04:04-04:05 long-term trim capture was not recorded - steady cruise was the instruction but the graph carries neither rpm nor speed, so it is not known which memory cell was displayed.
evidence: Closed by re-reading the idle cell at warm idle in Park, which was subsequently done and gave -0.78 / -0.78.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md '[VERIFY] The operating condition during this capture was not recorded'; CLAUDE.md; [249]

statement: THE LEAK IS CLOSED: long term trim at warm idle in Park reads -0.78 percent on BOTH banks - min = avg = max, dead flat across three consecutive windows, and identical to each other, not merely within one quantisation step.
evidence: LTFT - B1 paired with LTFT - B2, warm idle in Park, 04:28-04:31, after a full drive with relearned adaptives. This is the idle cell at the exact operating point where the symptom lives. Bank 1 moved 3.9 points, bank 2 moved 3.1 points. The engine no longer runs lean at idle by any amount.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE LEAK IS CLOSED'; CLAUDE.md; [251]

statement: The unmetered-air line of inquiry is FINISHED. PCV, brake booster, manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, injector O-rings and the smoke test are all withdrawn as suspects - there is no lean bias left for them to explain.
evidence: Idle trim -0.78 percent on both banks with relearned adaptives.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; CLAUDE.md; [251]

statement: The new purge valve behaves differently from the old one: EVAP purge now runs 47.06-49.80 percent, actively stepping up and down in single 0.39 percent increments over tens of seconds, where the old one sat flat at 40-41 percent drifting one LSB at a time. The PCM is genuinely controlling purge now.
evidence: Further evidence that the old valve was not responding to command. It does not drive the hunt - purge modulates over 10-30 s while the hunt runs at 3-4 s, and the two traces show no correlation across five paired windows.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The new purge valve behaves differently'; CLAUDE.md; [251]

statement: THE HUNT IS UNCHANGED after the repair: spans of 56, 51, 57, 67 and 61 rpm at the same ~3.4 s rhythm, if anything slightly wider than the 44-55 measured at 03:23 the same night. This is a clean separation - the leak is gone and the hunt did not change, so the leak was never causing the hunt.
evidence: Five consecutive windows, graph clock 12:37 to 13:47, warm idle in Park, 04:28-04:31.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The rpm hunt is UNCHANGED'; CLAUDE.md; [251]

statement: MODE 06 per-cylinder misfire (TID $0C): cylinder 1 = 0, 2 = 0, 3 = 0, 4 = 2, 5 = 0, 6 = 1, and the 10-cycle EWMA (TID $0B) is ZERO on all six. THE SINGLE-WEAK-CYLINDER HYPOTHESIS IS ELIMINATED - it was the last ECU-visible mechanism that could shake a cab with no code.
evidence: Read after the full drive that completed the monitors, 04:36-04:37. Manufacturer-defined TIDs $80 and $81 read 0 percent on every cylinder against limits of 30.98 and 0.949 percent. Two counts and one count across hundreds of thousands of firing events with a zero rolling average is noise; a genuinely weak cylinder produces tens to hundreds of counts and a non-zero average.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'MODE 06 - Per-cylinder misfire'; CLAUDE.md; [253];[254]

statement: A likely explanation for even those three misfire counts: the WOT pulls in the same session reached 6832 rpm, hitting the rev limiter, which cuts fuel and spark and can be logged by the misfire monitor as misfire events.
evidence: Optional confirmation: re-read Mode 06 after a drive containing no rev-limiter hits. Not done.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'A likely explanation'; [254]

statement: MODE 06 catalysts: bank 1 0.3711, bank 2 0.3633 against a 0.8359 limit - both PASSED at 44 percent of the failure threshold and within 2 percent of each other. This definitively kills the bank 1 downstream asymmetry recorded earlier from idle snapshots.
evidence: Catalyst Monitor MID$21 and MID$22, TID$81, read after the monitors completed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The catalyst question is settled'; CLAUDE.md; [254]

statement: RE-TEST after the repair: the commanded square wave is IDENTICAL. Levels 14.42 to 14.86 (first night 14.41 to 14.86), amplitude plus/minus 1.5 percent, period ~3.5 s (first night ~3.4 s). New purge valve, wiped and relearned adaptives, trims at -0.78 percent both banks - and the command is exactly what it was.

statement: The commanded ratio trace is a PERFECT TWO-LEVEL SQUARE WAVE with vertical edges - it sits at 14.86, drops to 14.42, returns, with nothing in between and an asymmetric dwell of roughly 2.5 s lean to 1 s rich. A control loop that is HUNTING produces a rounded continuous waveform; this is the PCM toggling between two fixed setpoints, a deliberate programmed function.
evidence: Shape read off the plotted curve across eight windows.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The SHAPE is the important new observation'; [259]

statement: RPM peaks roughly 1-1.5 s AFTER each rich command (rich at 37:01.5 gives an rpm peak at ~37:03; 37:05 gives ~37:06.5; 37:08.5 gives ~37:10) - command leads, rpm follows, the direction the theory predicts.
evidence: Cleanest window 37:00-37:15. Honest limit: not every window reads that cleanly - one contains a large excursion to 676 rpm that does not fit the pattern - and reading phase by eye in a closed loop remains suggestive rather than conclusive.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'RPM follows the command, with the right lag'; [259]

statement: THE READING THIS FORCES: it all looks NORMAL. Both upstream O2 sensors respond in 0.014 s against a 0.4 s limit; both catalysts sit at 44 percent of their limit; good oxygen storage makes the fore/aft loop SLOW, so a ~3.5 s period is what healthy converters produce (a degraded one would make the loop run faster); and plus/minus 1.5 percent commanded AFR is within what many Ford PCMs run. So yes, the ECU manipulates the rpm - deliberately, by design - and every measurable property of how it does so looks normal.
evidence: Mode 06 results combined with the re-tested command trace.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE READING THIS FORCES'; [259];[260]

statement: The cold start is the test that would settle causation: the dither is a closed-loop function and does not run at all in open loop, so capturing Engine RPM + Fuel/Air com. ratio from the first crank would show rpm steady while the command is flat, then hunting once the square wave begins. Hunting from cold, before any dither, and the theory is wrong.

statement: UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS that would explain the whole data set: is the rpm signal itself true? If the crankshaft position signal is noisy - marginal sensor, damaged connector, reluctor defect, twelve years of heat - the PCM would BELIEVE rpm is wandering, modulate spark to correct a phantom, and that spark modulation would make the engine genuinely oscillate. One fault producing static air, static fuel, parked cam, swinging spark, wandering rpm and a felt roughness.
evidence: Test by measuring engine speed independently of the PCM: a timing light with a tach function, an inductive tach on a plug lead, or the phone accelerometer (firing frequency = rpm/60 x 3). Never performed.

statement: Young adaptives are the likely contributor to the idle instability.

statement: A 2.5-4 second cycle is characteristic of the closed-loop fuel control loop whose speed is set by how fast the upstream oxygen sensors switch, so a slow sensor lengthens the loop - the O2 sensors are the leading suspect for the oscillation.
evidence: Reasoning about loop period. The O2 sensors on this truck were 'cleaned' by an unknown method.
reason_withdrawn: The sensors have since been measured and are fast, clean and symmetric across both banks (fuel cut sweep 13.49-29.38 and 12.33-29.38; Mode 06 response 0.014 s against a 0.4 s limit). The seconds-scale period belongs to the fore/aft catalyst control loop, whose dither the PCM commands deliberately.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What oscillates with a period of a few seconds - SUPERSEDED'

statement: The oxygen sensors were 'cleaned' by an unknown method, and heated O2 sensors are not serviceable by cleaning - solvent attacks the platinum layer and the ceramic element, and mechanical cleaning damages the shroud's diffusion slots. Either is permanent. Treat as a separate, owed repair.
evidence: Carried as a housekeeping item throughout the project, separate from the shake (the symptom is identical cold, where the PCM runs open loop and ignores them).
reason_withdrawn: Closed by measurement: the deceleration fuel cut showed both upstream sensors sweeping their full range fast in both directions, and Mode 06 gave 0.014 s response against a 0.4 s limit on both, with matched heater currents. All four sensors are healthy.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Concern: the oxygen sensors'; CLAUDE.md
